hints: Rewrite the integrand as $(\ln x)x^{-3}$ and use integration by parts.
Choose $u=\ln x$ and integrate $x^{-3}$ for the other part.
Simplify the remaining integral as a power of $x$.
Complete the power-rule integration and include an arbitrary constant.
walkthrough:
Use integration by parts $\int u\,\mathrm{d}v = uv - \int v\,\mathrm{d}u$ with:
$$u = \ln x \implies \mathrm{d}u = \dfrac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x$$
$$\mathrm{d}v = x^{-3}\,\mathrm{d}x \implies v = -\dfrac{1}{2x^2}$$

Assemble the integration by parts formula:
$$\int \dfrac{\ln x}{x^3}\,\mathrm{d}x = -\dfrac{\ln x}{2x^2} - \int \left(-\dfrac{1}{2x^2}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x$$
$$= -\dfrac{\ln x}{2x^2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\int x^{-3}\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Integrate the remaining power of $x$:
$$\dfrac{1}{2}\int x^{-3}\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2x^2}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{4x^2}$$

Combine terms and add the constant of integration:
$$-\dfrac{\ln x}{2x^2} - \dfrac{1}{4x^2} + C$$

hints: Use the antiderivative obtained in part (i) and substitute the upper and lower limits exactly.
At $x=1$, use $\ln1=0$; at $x=2$, keep the logarithm exact.
Subtract the lower-limit value in full before simplifying.
Use $2\ln2=\ln4$ to put the result into the required form.
walkthrough:
Subtract the lower limit value from the upper limit value:
$$\int_1^2 \dfrac{\ln x}{x^3}\,\mathrm{d}x = \left(-\dfrac{2\ln 2 + 1}{16}\right) - \left(-\dfrac{1}{4}\right) = \dfrac{4}{16} - \dfrac{2\ln 2 + 1}{16} = \dfrac{4 - (2\ln 2 + 1)}{16} = \dfrac{3 - 2\ln 2}{16}$$
